paragraphs.text: Lit., “fornications; prostitutions.” Heb., zenu·nimʹ, pl. See Ge 38:24; Eze 23:11, 29.
The royal city where the kings of northern Israel resided, although Samaria was their capital city. See 2Ki (8:29; 9:15, 25, 30-37; 10:1-11).
Meaning “She Was Not Shown Mercy.” Heb., Loʼ ru·chaʹmah.
Or, “that I should positively pardon them.”
Meaning “Not My People.” Heb., Loʼ ʽam·miʹ.
MLXX end chap. 1 here; TSyVg continue for two more vss.
Meaning “God Will Sow Seed.” Heb., Yiz·reʽeʼlʹ.
Lit., “She has been shown mercy.” Heb., ru·chaʹmah.
Or, “the Baals.” Heb., hab·Beʽa·limʹ; Gr., Ba·a·limʹ; Lat., Baʹa·lim.
Or, “and in loyal love.” Heb., u·vecheʹsedh.
“Know Jehovah,” MLXXSy; Vg and about 45 Heb. mss, “know that I am Jehovah.”
“Her who was not shown mercy.” Heb., loʼ ru·chaʹmah. See 1:6 ftn, “Lo-ruhamah.”
Or, “to the one not my people.” Heb., leloʼ-ʽam·miʹ. See 1:9 ftn, “Lo-ammi.”
Lit., “it itself,” referring to “people,” masc. sing.
“Loved by a companion,” MVg; LXXSy, “loving bad things.”
Or, “and committing marital sexual unfaithfulness.” Heb., u·mena·ʼaʹpheth; Gr., moi·kha·linʹ; Lat., a·dulʹte·ram. See Mt 5:32 ftn, “Adultery.”
“For another man,” LXX; M(Heb., leʼishʹ)SyVg, “to a man.”
Or, “will die”; or, “will be taken away.” See Isa 57:1.

“My own glory they have exchanged” was the original reading. The Sopherim emended (changed) the text to read, “Their own glory I will exchange.” TSy confirm the original reading of the verb. See App 2B.
“Their soul(s),” TLXXSyVg and about 20 Heb. mss; M, “his soul (soulful desire).” See App 4A.
“Fornication.” Heb., zenuthʹ; Gr., por·neiʹan; Lat., for·ni·caʹti·o. See App 5A.
Lit., “take away heart.” Heb., yiq·qach-levʹ. Compare interlinear reading of Grn.
Or, “A spirit.” Heb., ruʹach; Gr., pneuʹma·tos; Lat., spiʹri·tus.
That is, a straight trumpet. Heb., chatso·tserahʹ; not the shofar, which was a ram’s curved horn. See Nu 10:2.
“His adversary,” by a correction; M, “a commandment”; LXXSy, “vanities”; Vg, “filth.”
Or, “King Jareb.” Lit., “a king [that] should contend.”
Or, “without good motive.” Heb., ʼehn lev.
“Not to anything higher.” Lit., “not upward,” that is, not to an elevated form of worship. Heb., loʼ ʽal.
“God.” Heb., ʼElo·himʹ; Gr., The·osʹ; Lat., Deʹus.
“Wind.” Heb., ruʹach; Lat., venʹtum. See Ge 1:2 ftn, “Force.”
Or, “for their own selves.” Heb., lenaph·shamʹ; Gr., tais psy·khaisʹ au·tonʹ; Lat., aʹni·mae i·psoʹrum. See App 4A.
“Memphis.” Gr. and Lat., Memʹphis; Heb., Moph; T(Aram.), leMa·phehsʹ; Syr., u·Ma·phes.
Or, “man of inspiration.” Lit., “man of the spirit.” Heb., ʼish ha·ruʹach; Gr., anʹthro·pos ho pneu·ma·to·phoʹros, “man bearing the spirit; man inspired”; Vgc(Lat.), viʹrum spi·ri·tu·aʹlem.
Lit., “They have made [it] deep, they have brought [it] to ruin,” M; possibly, by a correction, “They have made his pit deep.”
Or, “to withdraw themselves to; to hold themselves separate for.”
“Luxuriant; outspreading,” if derived from another Heb. verb of the same form.
“As well as its foreign-god priests.” Heb., u·khema·ravʹ, “Chemarim”; Vg, “temple keepers.”
“From before them (from their faces),” MTVg; LXXSy, “from my face.”
Or, “To the Baals.” Heb., lab·Beʽa·limʹ; Gr., Ba·a·limʹ; Lat., Baʹa·lim.
“My,” in agreement with LXXSyVg; M, “his,” or, “one’s.”
In M both “it” and “people” are masc.
Or, “does any exalting.” Compare Ex 15:2; Ps 145:1, where the same Heb. verb occurs. In reality no one was exalting God.
“Man.” Heb., ʼish; Gr., anʹthro·pos; Lat., hoʹmo.
“The Most Holy One.” Heb., Qedhoh·shimʹ, pl. of qa·dhohshʹ, “holy”; pl. to denote excellence according to GK, § 124 h. Compare Pr 9:10 and Pr 30:3 ftns.
Or, “even with the Most Holy One, who is trustworthy.”
“The God of the armies,” MVg; LXX, “the God almighty.”
Or, “Canaanite.” Heb., kenaʹʽan; Gr., Kha·na·anʹ; Lat., Chaʹna·an. See Zec 14:21 ftn.
“With Gilead,” by a slight correction; M, “If Gilead.”
“His grand Master.” Heb., ʼAdho·navʹ, pl. of ʼA·dhohnʹ, to denote excellence or grandeur, accompanied by the sing. verb “repay.” Compare Ge 39:2 ftn.
“Sheol.” Heb., sheʼohlʹ; Gr., haiʹdou; Lat., morʹtis, “death.” See App 4B.
“From death.” Heb., mim·maʹweth; Gr., ek tha·naʹtou; Lat., de morʹte.
Or, “I shall repurchase them.” Heb., ʼegh·ʼa·lemʹ.
“O Sheol.” Heb., sheʼohlʹ; Gr., haiʹde; Lat., in·ferʹne.
“Wind.” Heb., ruʹach; Lat., venʹtum. See Ge 1:2 ftn, “Force.”
“The young bulls of our lips,” MVg; LXX, “the fruit of our lips.”
Or, “I shall prove to be.” Compare Ex 3:14 ftn.
“His memorial.” Or, “The mention of Him.” Heb., zikh·rohʹ.
Lit., “What to me yet to the idols?” A Heb. idiom; a repellent question to indicate objection to the idols. See App 7B.
